people.name: Steve Wozniak
people.role: Co-Founder of Apple & Mental Health Advocate
people.bio: Steve Wozniak is an engineer, inventor and co-founder of Apple. His philanthropic interests include education, creativity and innovation, and he co-founded the Wozniak Family Foundation with Janet Wozniak.

people.name: Jewel
people.role: 4-Time Grammy Nominated Singer-Songwriter and Mental Health Pioneer
people.bio: Jewel is a singer-songwriter and mental health advocate. Inspiring Children recognizes her work in music and human development and lists her among the gathering's co-chairs.

people.name: Cherrial Odell
people.bio: Cherrial Odell is an Inspiring Children Foundation alumna. She is listed as a co-chair on the foundation's public Summit website and is an owner-confirmed co-chair for the 2026 gathering.

people.name: Loni Love
people.bio: Loni Love is a comedian and television host. She is the host of the 2026 Not Alone Awards, bringing her experience in entertainment to the celebration of human development and mental health.

people.name: Nick Kislinger
people.bio: Nick Kislinger works across philanthropy, social innovation and mental health. His public ICF biography describes his work advising charitable initiatives, co-founding Impact Hub Los Angeles and launching the breathwork app Breathwrk.

people.name: Ellie Kanner
people.bio: Ellie Kanner is a director, writer and producer whose career also includes casting for Friends and Sex and the City. Her directing credits include Authors Anonymous, Wake and the series Dropping the Soap.

people.name: Melinda & Noah Springer
people.bio: Melinda and Noah Springer are recognized together among the founders on Inspiring Children Foundation's public Awards website, with their affiliation listed as Pickle Pro Labs.

people.name: Jen Smorgen
people.bio: Jennifer Smorgon is a meditation teacher and mentor, and a founding member of the Chopra Foundation. She has taught in corporate and community settings and helps make meditation accessible in daily life.

people.name: Sean & Ana Wolfington
people.bio: Sean and Ana Wolfington are entrepreneurs and philanthropists. Inspiring Children Foundation's public Awards and Summit materials recognize their shared philanthropic work and support for youth development.

people.name: Janet Wozniak
people.bio: Janet Wozniak has worked in education development at Apple. With Steve Wozniak, she co-founded the Wozniak Family Foundation to support STEM education and social development.

people.name: Anthony Ramos
people.bio: Anthony Ramos is an actor and recording artist. He originated the roles of John Laurens and Philip Hamilton in Hamilton and played the lead role in the film adaptation of In the Heights.

people.name: Caroline Jones
people.bio: Caroline Jones is a singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist with a solo recording career and experience as a member of Zac Brown Band. Her work spans country music and collaborations with fellow artists.

people.name: Alana Springsteen
people.bio: Alana Springsteen is a country singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. She plays guitar and piano, co-produces her music and draws on personal experience in her songwriting.

people.name: Darryl McDaniels (DMC)
people.bio: Darryl McDaniels, known as DMC, is a musician associated with Run-DMC. Inspiring Children's public Awards website includes him in its Musicians category.

people.name: Jason Kennedy
people.bio: Jason Kennedy is an entertainment journalist. Inspiring Children's public Awards website lists him among entertainers and athletes, while its Summit website also recognizes him as Summit host.

people.name: Lexi Hensler
people.bio: Lexi Hensler is a digital content creator. Her public channels include YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, and her official links include the Hugz brand.

people.name: Brandon Saho
people.bio: Brandon Saho is a former sports reporter and the creator of The Mental Game. Through interviews and public conversations, he works to reduce stigma around mental health.

people.name: Bob Bryan
people.bio: Bob Bryan is a Hall of Fame tennis player. Inspiring Children's public Awards website recognizes Bob and Mike Bryan together in its Entertainers & Athletes category.

people.name: Mike Bryan
people.bio: Mike Bryan is a Hall of Fame tennis player. Inspiring Children's public Awards website recognizes Mike and Bob Bryan together in its Entertainers & Athletes category.

people.name: Mike Tyson
people.bio: Mike Tyson is a Hall of Fame boxer. His career in professional boxing is recognized on Inspiring Children's public Awards website, which includes him among entertainers and athletes.

people.name: Sarah Gilman
people.bio: Sarah Gilman is an actress. Inspiring Children's public Awards website includes her among its entertainers and athletes.

people.name: Jon Hershfield
people.bio: Jon Hershfield is a therapist specializing in obsessive-compulsive disorder and anxiety. His work combines exposure-based therapy with mindfulness and self-compassion, and he has authored and co-authored several books on OCD.

people.name: Wendy Oliver-Pyatt
people.bio: Wendy Oliver-Pyatt is an eating disorder expert. Inspiring Children's public Awards website recognizes her clinical expertise in its Experts category.

people.name: Caroline Silby
people.bio: Caroline Silby is a sport psychologist who works with athletes on mental performance. Her experience includes supporting U.S. Figure Skating and athletes competing at the Olympic level.

people.name: Marc Brackett
people.bio: Marc Brackett is listed as a Yale-affiliated expert on Inspiring Children's public Awards website. His inclusion connects the gathering with research and expertise in emotional and mental well-being.

people.name: David Eagleman
people.bio: David Eagleman is a neuroscientist and author whose research includes perception and sensory substitution. His books include Livewired and Incognito, and he has explored the relationship between neuroscience and the legal system.

people.name: Blaise Aguirre
people.bio: Blaise Aguirre is a child and adolescent psychiatrist at McLean Hospital. His work includes dialectical behavior therapy and the 3East programs for adolescents, and he has written books on treatment and mindfulness.

people.name: Mike Majlak
people.bio: Mike Majlak is a media personality associated with the Impaulsive podcast. Inspiring Children's public Awards website includes him among business leaders and philanthropists.

people.name: Kevin Hines
people.bio: Kevin Hines is a mental health advocate, author and speaker focused on suicide prevention and resilience. His work includes the Kevin & Margaret Hines Foundation and the book Cracked, Not Broken.

people.name: Daniel Gillison
people.bio: Daniel Gillison is associated with the National Alliance on Mental Illness, known as NAMI. Inspiring Children's public Awards website recognizes him in its Business Leaders & Philanthropists category.

people.name: Ryan Wolfington
people.bio: Ryan Wolfington is a founder of Inspiring Children Foundation. The foundation's public Summit website credits him as an executive producer of the gathering.

people.name: Trevor Short
people.bio: Trevor Short is a founder of Inspiring Dreams. Inspiring Children's public Summit website recognizes him among the gathering's executive producers.

people.name: Aphrah Brokaw
people.bio: Aphrah Brokaw is a music manager associated with Jewel Inc. Inspiring Children's public Summit website recognizes her work as a producer of the gathering.

people.name: Trent Alenik
people.bio: Trent Alenik is identified by Inspiring Children Foundation as its CEO. The foundation's public Summit website also credits him as a producer of the gathering.

awards.venue: Encore Theater at Wynn Las Vegas
awards.intro: The award show was created to celebrate the pioneers of human development and mental health, the visionaries, healers, and innovators who have courageously broken barriers, challenged stigma, and illuminated the path toward healing, growth, and connection.

host.name: Loni Love
host.bio: Loni Love is a comedian and television host. She is the host of the 2026 Not Alone Awards, bringing her experience in entertainment to the celebration of human development and mental health.
